What makes the strawberry so fascinating?

Red and sweet, the strawberry is a favorite fruit for kids. But did you know that the red part we eat isn't actually the real fruit?

content.alt: Strawberry - Nature and science facts about the strawberry
content.text:
Nature and science facts about the strawberry

The red, sweet part of a strawberry is actually a false fruit (the receptacle) that grew from a swollen flower base. The real fruits are the tiny yellow dots (achenes) studded across the surface, each holding a seed inside. Besides its seeds, the strawberry also sends out runners along the ground to make new plants. Good pollination by bees is what makes big, pretty strawberries.

Great things to observe together

Point out details like the yellow dots on the outside (the real seeds), the red part (the false fruit), the runners (reproduction), and the white flowers. It's a great idea to talk together about, "Where are a strawberry's seeds?"

Parent guide — extending into observation and hands-on activities

Count the yellow dots (the seeds) on a strawberry's surface with a magnifying glass. Explain that "the red part is the fake one, and the dots are the real fruit," and it's a good idea to watch the runners spreading from a potted strawberry plant.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Where are a strawberry's seeds?
A. Each tiny yellow dot studded on the surface is a real fruit (an achene), with a seed inside.

Q. What is the red part we eat?
A. It's a false fruit (the receptacle) that grew from a swollen flower base. The real fruits are the dots on the outside.

Q. How can we observe this at home?
A. Try counting the dots on a strawberry's surface with a magnifier, and observing the runners on a potted strawberry plant.
